note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

precepts.why:
“Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.”

Rehoboam rejects the safe counsel of the elders: “he forsook the counsel which the old men gave him, and took counsel with the young men that were brought up with him, that stood before him.” He asks them, “What advice give ye that we may return answer to this people”, including them as if they were rulers with him over the nation.

This is the same error seen constantly among the people: one comes to the truth and seeks counsel from a new brother or sister rather than from the elder men and women already established in the congregation. And the young men's counsel was rough: “My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s loins”, “I will put more to your yoke: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.”

precepts.text: The Lord, angry that Solomon's heart turned to other gods, declares he will rend the kingdom from him and give it to his servant; this is the prophecy now being fulfilled.
precepts.point: The king does not listen to the people, for the cause was of the Most High, that the Lord might fulfill the word spoken by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

precepts.why:
“And the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel, which had appeared unto him twice.” He had commanded Solomon “that he should not go after other gods: but he kept not that which the Lord commanded.”

So the Lord said, “I will surely rend the kingdom from thee, and will give it to thy servant.” That is the prophecy now being fulfilled. When Rehoboam answered the people roughly and hearkened not unto them, “the cause was of God, that the Lord might perform his word, which he spake by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.”

points: Rehoboam tells them to come again after three days.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: Rehoboam goes to Shechem where all Israel has gathered to make him king, and Jeroboam the son of Nebat returns out of Egypt where he had fled from Solomon.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: The people, led by Jeroboam, ask Rehoboam to ease the grievous yoke and heavy service his father laid on them, promising then to serve him.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: Rehoboam first takes counsel with the old men who stood before Solomon while his father lived, asking what answer to return.
This is the wise counsel he should have followed, coming from the elders who had experience in place before him.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: They advise him that if he is kind to the people, pleases them, and speaks good words, they will be his servants forever.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: Rehoboam forsakes the counsel of the old men and turns to the young men brought up with him, including them as if they were rulers with him over the nation.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: This is the same error seen constantly among the people: one comes to the truth and seeks counsel from a new brother or sister rather than from the elder men and women already established in the congregation.
The young men advise him to answer roughly, saying his little finger will be thicker than his father's loins, that he will add to their yoke, and chastise them with scorpions instead of whips.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: Jeroboam and the people return on the third day, and the king answers them roughly, forsaking the counsel of the old men and following the young men.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: He tells them he will add to their heavy yoke and chastise them with scorpions.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: The king does not listen to the people, for the cause was of the Most High, that the Lord might fulfill the word spoken by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: When all Israel sees the king will not listen, they answer that they have no portion in David nor inheritance in the son of Jesse, and every man departs to his tent.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: Rehoboam still reigns over the children of Israel who dwell in the cities of Judah, but when he sends Hadoram over the tribute, Israel stones him to death.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: Rehoboam flees by chariot to Jerusalem, and Israel rebels against the house of David to this day; the same division between the kingdoms persists.
